## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

The *Dutiyamigaluddakapetavatthu* ("The Deer-Hunter [2nd]", Pv 33) is a short narrative preserved in the *Petavatthu* of the Khuddaka Nikāya [SuttaCentral]. The core theme of the text demonstrates that taking the life of living beings inexorably leads to rebirth in misery and profound suffering [SuttaCentral]. Four modern translations in four languages are recorded on SuttaCentral [SuttaCentral].
Within the Pali tradition, the text exhibits significant internal text reuse with its preceding companion narrative, the *Migaluddakapetavatthu* (Pv 32), sharing three major passages including an extended sequence (§4.4–12.1 aligned with Pv 32 §3.4–11.1) [DharmaNexus]. The text is also extensively embedded and commented upon in the *Petavatthu-aṭṭhakathā*, which shares 25 matching segments [DharmaNexus]. Although SuttaCentral does not record any curated cross-canonical parallels [SuttaCentral], automated text-reuse analysis via DharmaNexus identifies notable Sanskrit alignments in the *Carmavastu* of the Vinaya (§5.2) and the *Divyāvadāna* (§5.2–5.6), alongside low-scoring alignments with the Tibetan translation of the *Ārya-mañjuśrīmūlatantra* [DharmaNexus].
